claim: Peripheral sensory neurons are traditionally assumed as the exclusive transducers of external stimuli.
source: Traditionally, peripheral sensory neurons are assumed as the exclusive transducers of external stimuli.
evidence: This is a statement about traditional scientific understanding presented in the abstract without specific supporting data in this manuscript.

claim: Current research moves epidermal keratinocytes into focus as sensors and transmitters of nociceptive and non-nociceptive sensations.
source: Current research moves epidermal keratinocytes into focus as sensors and transmitters of nociceptive and non-nociceptive sensations, tightly interacting with intraepidermal nerve fibers at the neuro-cutaneous unit.
evidence: This statement references current research trends without specific citations in this sentence.

claim: In animal models, epidermal cells establish close contacts and ensheath sensory neurites.
source: In animal models, epidermal cells establish close contacts and ensheath sensory neurites.
evidence: This statement references findings from animal models as established knowledge.

claim: Ultrastructural morphological and mechanistic data examining the human keratinocyte-nerve fiber interface are sparse.
source: However, ultrastructural morphological and mechanistic data examining the human keratinocyte-nerve fiber interface are sparse.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of the field that motivates the current study.

claim: Super-resolution array tomography reveals keratinocyte ensheathment of afferents in human skin.
source: We show keratinocyte ensheathment of afferents and adjacent connexin 43 contacts in native skin and have applied a pipeline based on expansion microscopy to quantify these parameter in skin sections of healthy participants versus patients with small fiber neuropathy.
evidence: This claim is supported by the srAT imaging data presented in Figure 1.

claim: Connexin 43 contacts are present adjacent to afferents in native human skin.
source: We show keratinocyte ensheathment of afferents and adjacent connexin 43 contacts in native skin and have applied a pipeline based on expansion microscopy to quantify these parameter in skin sections of healthy participants versus patients with small fiber neuropathy.
evidence: This claim is supported by the srAT and ExM imaging data presented in Figures 3 and 4.

claim: A fully human co-culture system of keratinocytes and sensory neurons shows ensheathment and connexin 43 plaques in vitro.
source: We further derived a fully human co-culture system, visualizing ensheathment and connexin 43 plaques in vitro.
evidence: This claim is supported by the co-culture data presented in Figures 6-8.

claim: Impairment of thinly-myelinated A-delta and unmyelinated C-nerve fibers may underlie small nerve fiber pathology in patients with peripheral nervous system diseases.
source: Impairment of the thinly-melinated A-delta and unmyelinated C-nerve fibers may underlie small nerve fiber pathology observed in patients with peripheral (Birklein, 2005; Lacomis, 2002; Üçeyler et al., 2013) and central nervous system diseases (Nolano et al., 2008; Weis et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: Impairment of thinly-myelinated A-delta and unmyelinated C-nerve fibers may underlie small nerve fiber pathology in patients with central nervous system diseases.
source: Impairment of the thinly-melinated A-delta and unmyelinated C-nerve fibers may underlie small nerve fiber pathology observed in patients with peripheral (Birklein, 2005; Lacomis, 2002; Üçeyler et al., 2013) and central nervous system diseases (Nolano et al., 2008; Weis et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Cutaneous nerve fiber degeneration and sensitization are hallmarks of small fiber pathology.
source: Cutaneous nerve fiber degeneration and sensitization are hallmarks of small fiber pathology; however, the underlying pathomechanisms are unclear (Üçeyler, 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: The underlying pathomechanisms of small fiber pathology are unclear.
source: Cutaneous nerve fiber degeneration and sensitization are hallmarks of small fiber pathology; however, the underlying pathomechanisms are unclear (Üçeyler, 2016).
evidence: This statement about the state of knowledge is supported by a citation.

claim: The impact of skin cells on nociceptive and non-nociceptive stimulus detection is increasingly recognized.
source: The impact of skin cells on nociceptive and non-nociceptive stimulus detection is increasingly recognized (Lumpkin and Caterina, 2007; Stucky and Mikesell, 2021).
evidence: This claim about a research trend is supported by citations.

claim: Keratinocytes are the predominant cell type in the epidermis.
source: Physiologically, keratinocytes are the predominant cell type in the epidermis and actively participate in sensory signal transduction and nociception at the neuro-cutaneous unit (NCU).
evidence: This is a statement of established anatomical knowledge.

claim: Keratinocytes actively participate in sensory signal transduction and nociception at the neuro-cutaneous unit.
source: Physiologically, keratinocytes are the predominant cell type in the epidermis and actively participate in sensory signal transduction and nociception at the neuro-cutaneous unit (NCU).
evidence: This is a general statement about keratinocyte function that is elaborated with specific citations in subsequent sentences.

claim: Selective thermal, chemical, or mechanical keratinocyte stimulation led to activation of co-cultured peripheral neurons in animal in vitro cell culture models.
source: In animal in vitro cell culture models, selective thermal, chemical, or mechanical keratinocyte stimulation led to activation of co-cultured peripheral neurons (Klusch et al., 2013; Mandadi et al., 2009; Sondersorg et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior experimental work.

claim: Nociceptive behavior was induced in mice selectively expressing TRPV1 in keratinocytes after capsaicin treatment.
source: Using animal models, nociceptive behavior was induced in mice selectively expressing transient receptor potential vanilloid 1 (TRPV1) in keratinocytes after capsaicin treatment (Pang et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a specific animal study.

claim: Mice expressing channelrhodopsin-2 in keratinocytes displayed pain behavior during laser stimulation.
source: Mice expressing channelrhodopsin-2 in keratinocytes also displayed pain behavior and intraepidermal nerve fiber (IENF) derived evoked nerve fiber action potentials during laser stimulation (Baumbauer et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a specific animal study.

claim: Mice expressing channelrhodopsin-2 in keratinocytes displayed IENF derived evoked nerve fiber action potentials during laser stimulation.
source: Mice expressing channelrhodopsin-2 in keratinocytes also displayed pain behavior and intraepidermal nerve fiber (IENF) derived evoked nerve fiber action potentials during laser stimulation (Baumbauer et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a specific animal study.

claim: Knockout of the mechanoreceptor PIEZO1 in keratinocytes attenuated both innocuous and noxious touch sensation in mice.
source: Further, knockout of the mechanoreceptor PIEZO1 in keratinocytes attenuated both innocuous and noxious touch sensation in mice (Mikesell et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a specific animal study.

claim: ATP is increasingly recognized as a signaling molecule for functional stimulus transduction between keratinocytes and IENF.
source: For underlying functional stimulus transduction of keratinocytes and IENF, signaling molecules such as ATP are increasingly recognized (Mandadi et al., 2009; Moehring et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Hemichannels or gap junctions formed by connexins and pannexins may conduct ATP signaling toward afferent nerve fibers.
source: Hemichannels or gap junctions formed by connexins and pannexins, or vesicular transport may conduct ATP signaling toward afferent nerve fibers (Barr et al., 2013; Maruyama et al., 2018; Sondersorg et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Vesicular transport may conduct ATP signaling toward afferent nerve fibers.
source: Hemichannels or gap junctions formed by connexins and pannexins, or vesicular transport may conduct ATP signaling toward afferent nerve fibers (Barr et al., 2013; Maruyama et al., 2018; Sondersorg et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Connexin 43 pores are well established as a major signaling route for keratinocyte-keratinocyte communication.
source: Connexin 43 (Cx43) pores are well established as a major signaling route for keratinocyte-keratinocyte communication (Tsutsumi et al., 2009) and potentially transduce external stimuli likewise toward afferents.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Connexin 43 pores potentially transduce external stimuli toward afferents.
source: Connexin 43 (Cx43) pores are well established as a major signaling route for keratinocyte-keratinocyte communication (Tsutsumi et al., 2009) and potentially transduce external stimuli likewise toward afferents.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential function based on inference from known keratinocyte-keratinocyte communication.

claim: Signaling might happen via specialized synapse-like connections to IENF.
source: Signaling might also happen via specialized synapse-like connections to IENF (Talagas et al., 2020a).
evidence: This speculative claim is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: In Danio rerio models, nerve endings are frequently ensheathed by epidermal cells.
source: In Danio rerio and Drosophila models, nerve endings are frequently ensheathed by epidermal cells (Jiang et al., 2019; O'Brien et al., 2012) and tunneling of fibers through keratinocytes in human skin has recently been shown via confocal microscopy (Talagas et al., 2020b).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior animal model studies.

claim: In Drosophila models, nerve endings are frequently ensheathed by epidermal cells.
source: In Danio rerio and Drosophila models, nerve endings are frequently ensheathed by epidermal cells (Jiang et al., 2019; O'Brien et al., 2012) and tunneling of fibers through keratinocytes in human skin has recently been shown via confocal microscopy (Talagas et al., 2020b).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior animal model studies.

claim: Tunneling of fibers through keratinocytes in human skin has recently been shown via confocal microscopy.
source: In Danio rerio and Drosophila models, nerve endings are frequently ensheathed by epidermal cells (Jiang et al., 2019; O'Brien et al., 2012) and tunneling of fibers through keratinocytes in human skin has recently been shown via confocal microscopy (Talagas et al., 2020b).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior human tissue study.

claim: The exact mechanisms and mode of signal transduction at the NCU remain elusive.
source: However, the exact mechanisms and mode of signal transduction at the NCU remain elusive.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge that motivates the study.

claim: Physical contacts between sensory neurons and keratinocytes were observed in an embryonic stem-cell-derived 2D human cell culture model.
source: In an embryonic stem-cell-derived 2D human cell culture model, physical contacts between sensory neurons and keratinocytes were observed hinting to close coupling (Krishnan-Kutty et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior cell culture work.

claim: Direct and systematic information on ensheathment of human IENF is scarce.
source: Still, direct and systematic information on ensheathment of human IENF is scarce and ultrastructural architecture or molecular processes remain obscure.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of the field that motivates the current study.

claim: Ultrastructural architecture or molecular processes at the human keratinocyte-IENF interface remain obscure.
source: Still, direct and systematic information on ensheathment of human IENF is scarce and ultrastructural architecture or molecular processes remain obscure.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of the field that motivates the current study.

claim: Altered keratinocyte signal molecule release may contribute to cutaneous pain perception.
source: Ultimately, altered keratinocyte signal molecule release or dysfunctional signaling sites may contribute to cutaneous pain perception (Talagas et al., 2018), which could open novel avenues for neuroprotective, regenerative, and analgesic treatment of patients with small fiber pathology (Keppel Hesselink et al., 2017).
evidence: This speculative claim is supported by a citation.

claim: Dysfunctional signaling sites may contribute to cutaneous pain perception.
source: Ultimately, altered keratinocyte signal molecule release or dysfunctional signaling sites may contribute to cutaneous pain perception (Talagas et al., 2018), which could open novel avenues for neuroprotective, regenerative, and analgesic treatment of patients with small fiber pathology (Keppel Hesselink et al., 2017).
evidence: This speculative claim is supported by a citation.

claim: Understanding keratinocyte-IENF interactions could open novel avenues for neuroprotective, regenerative, and analgesic treatment of patients with small fiber pathology.
source: Ultimately, altered keratinocyte signal molecule release or dysfunctional signaling sites may contribute to cutaneous pain perception (Talagas et al., 2018), which could open novel avenues for neuroprotective, regenerative, and analgesic treatment of patients with small fiber pathology (Keppel Hesselink et al., 2017).
evidence: This speculative claim about potential therapeutic implications is supported by a citation.

claim: Super-resolution array tomography in high-pressure frozen, freeze substituted samples revealed ensheathment in native human skin.
source: A correlative light and electron microscopy (CLEM) approach via super-resolution array tomography (srAT) in high-pressure frozen, freeze substituted samples (Markert et al., 2017) and expansion microscopy (ExM) (Tillberg et al., 2016) in diagnostic paraformaldehyde-fixed tissue sections revealed ensheathment and pore protein Cx43 plaques in native human skin.
evidence: This claim is supported by the experimental data presented in Figure 1 and cites the methodology.

claim: Expansion microscopy in diagnostic paraformaldehyde-fixed tissue sections revealed ensheathment in native human skin.
source: A correlative light and electron microscopy (CLEM) approach via super-resolution array tomography (srAT) in high-pressure frozen, freeze substituted samples (Markert et al., 2017) and expansion microscopy (ExM) (Tillberg et al., 2016) in diagnostic paraformaldehyde-fixed tissue sections revealed ensheathment and pore protein Cx43 plaques in native human skin.
evidence: This claim is supported by the experimental data presented in Figures 2, 4, and 5 and cites the methodology.

claim: Super-resolution array tomography revealed Cx43 plaques in native human skin.
source: A correlative light and electron microscopy (CLEM) approach via super-resolution array tomography (srAT) in high-pressure frozen, freeze substituted samples (Markert et al., 2017) and expansion microscopy (ExM) (Tillberg et al., 2016) in diagnostic paraformaldehyde-fixed tissue sections revealed ensheathment and pore protein Cx43 plaques in native human skin.
evidence: This claim is supported by the experimental data presented in Figure 3 and cites the methodology.

claim: Expansion microscopy revealed Cx43 plaques in native human skin.
source: A correlative light and electron microscopy (CLEM) approach via super-resolution array tomography (srAT) in high-pressure frozen, freeze substituted samples (Markert et al., 2017) and expansion microscopy (ExM) (Tillberg et al., 2016) in diagnostic paraformaldehyde-fixed tissue sections revealed ensheathment and pore protein Cx43 plaques in native human skin.
evidence: This claim is supported by the experimental data presented in Figures 4 and 5 and cites the methodology.

claim: Ensheathment is present in vitro at the NCU in a fully human keratinocyte and sensory neuron co-culture system.
source: Both phenomena were also present in vitro at the NCU in a fully human keratinocyte and sensory neuron co-culture system which we succeeded to establish.
evidence: This claim is supported by the co-culture data presented in Figures 7 and 8.

claim: Cx43-based keratinocyte-nerve fiber contacts are present in vitro at the NCU in a fully human keratinocyte and sensory neuron co-culture system.
source: Both phenomena were also present in vitro at the NCU in a fully human keratinocyte and sensory neuron co-culture system which we succeeded to establish.
evidence: This claim is supported by the co-culture data presented in Figure 7.

claim: Many IENF were passing between neighboring keratinocytes.
source: While many IENF were passing between neighboring keratinocytes, srAT revealed IENF ensheathed by keratinocytes in skin samples of all three healthy subjects.
evidence: This observation is supported by the srAT imaging data in Figure 1.

claim: srAT revealed IENF ensheathed by keratinocytes in skin samples of all three healthy subjects.
source: While many IENF were passing between neighboring keratinocytes, srAT revealed IENF ensheathed by keratinocytes in skin samples of all three healthy subjects.
evidence: This claim is directly supported by the srAT imaging data presented in Figure 1.

claim: Tunneling of fibers was observed both in the basal and upper epidermal layers.
source: This tunneling of fibers was observed both in the basal and upper epidermal layers for several consecutive 100-nm-thin sections indicated via PGP9.5 labeling (Figure 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by the imaging data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: IENF intersected closely to either the lateral, posterior, or anterior boundary of the respective keratinocyte.
source: IENF intersected closely to either the lateral, posterior, or anterior boundary of the respective keratinocyte and was engulfed by the respective cell for several µm (Figure 1A, Figure 1—video 1).
evidence: This observation is supported by the imaging data in Figure 1A and associated video.

claim: IENF was engulfed by the respective keratinocyte for several µm.
source: IENF intersected closely to either the lateral, posterior, or anterior boundary of the respective keratinocyte and was engulfed by the respective cell for several µm (Figure 1A, Figure 1—video 1).
evidence: This quantitative observation is supported by the imaging data in Figure 1A and associated video.

claim: A major part of the respective nerve fiber grew in close contact to and in between keratinocytes.
source: Whilst a major part of the respective nerve fiber grew in close contact to and in between keratinocytes, a substantial portion tunneled through one basal keratinocyte.
evidence: This observation is supported by the 3D reconstruction data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: A substantial portion of the nerve fiber tunneled through one basal keratinocyte.
source: Whilst a major part of the respective nerve fiber grew in close contact to and in between keratinocytes, a substantial portion tunneled through one basal keratinocyte.
evidence: This observation is supported by the 3D reconstruction data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: High pressure freezing and freeze substitution followed by LR-White embedding preserved the ultrastructure and antigenicity of the human skin tissue.
source: High pressure freezing and freeze substitution followed by LR-White embedding preserved the ultrastructure and antigenicity of the human skin tissue as illustrated by identification of collagen fibrils, desmosomes, nuclei, and mitochondria (Figure 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by the imaging data showing preserved cellular structures in Figure 1C.

claim: Expansion factor of samples fell between 4.3 and 4.4 x.
source: Expansion factor of samples fell between 4.3 and 4.4 x and showed isotropic epidermal expansion as documented via pre- and post-expansion acquired images (Figure 2).
evidence: This quantitative measurement is supported by the pre- and post-expansion imaging data in Figure 2.

claim: Samples showed isotropic epidermal expansion.
source: Expansion factor of samples fell between 4.3 and 4.4 x and showed isotropic epidermal expansion as documented via pre- and post-expansion acquired images (Figure 2).
evidence: This observation is supported by the pre- and post-expansion imaging data in Figure 2.

claim: Nerve fibers were traced via ExM for their course through the epidermis, being ensheathed over several µm.
source: Nerve fibers were traced via ExM for their course through the epidermis, being ensheathed over several µm (Figure 2—video 1).
evidence: This observation is supported by the ExM imaging data in Figure 2 and associated video.

claim: IENF-specific co-localization with TRPV1 could not be extracted after expansion.
source: To discriminate IENF subtypes, we applied immunoreaction against TRPV1, however, we could not extract IENF-specific co-localization, also after expansion (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This negative result is supported by the imaging data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Connexin hexamers can form hemichannels acting as small pores.
source: Connexin hexamers can form hemichannels acting as small pores.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about connexin structure and function.

claim: In open state, small molecules can pass and be released from connexin hemichannels.
source: In open state, small molecules can pass and be released from the cell, which was already shown for ATP and Cx43 (Weber et al., 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: ATP can pass and be released from Cx43 hemichannels.
source: In open state, small molecules can pass and be released from the cell, which was already shown for ATP and Cx43 (Weber et al., 2004).
evidence: This specific claim is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Cx43 hemichannels may allow purinergic signaling toward neighboring cells or nerve terminals in close proximity.
source: This may allow purinergic signaling toward neighboring cells or nerve terminals in close proximity.
evidence: This is an inference based on the known function of Cx43 hemichannels and their observed location near nerve fibers.

claim: Cx43 clusters were mostly found at keratinocyte-keratinocyte contact zones.
source: These clusters were mostly found at keratinocyte-keratinocyte contact zones (Figure 3A); however, distinct Cx43 plaques were also identified in direct proximity to single IENF when growing between keratinocytes (Figure 3B).
evidence: This observation is supported by the srAT imaging data in Figure 3A.

claim: Distinct Cx43 plaques were identified in direct proximity to single IENF when growing between keratinocytes.
source: These clusters were mostly found at keratinocyte-keratinocyte contact zones (Figure 3A); however, distinct Cx43 plaques were also identified in direct proximity to single IENF when growing between keratinocytes (Figure 3B).
evidence: This observation is supported by the srAT imaging data in Figure 3B.

claim: After expansion, specific Cx43-positive accumulations in direct contact to PGP9.5-positive IENF could be identified.
source: However, after expansion, specific Cx43-positive accumulations in direct contact to PGP9.5-positive IENF could be identified (Figure 4; see also Figure 2—video 1).

claim: The median expansion factor was 3.83±0.36.

evidence: This quantitative measurement is supported by the analysis shown in Figure 5B.

claim: The pixel count of PGP9.5 without WGA co-localization was 65.05% ± 14.51% for control samples.
source: After segmentation, the pixel count of PGP9.5 without WGA co-localization, as a correlate for ensheathment was 65.05% ± 14.51% for control samples and 50.82% ± 28.03% for SFN and did not differ between both groups (Figure 5C).
evidence: This quantitative measurement is supported by the analysis shown in Figure 5C.

claim: The pixel count of PGP9.5 without WGA co-localization was 50.82% ± 28.03% for SFN.
source: After segmentation, the pixel count of PGP9.5 without WGA co-localization, as a correlate for ensheathment was 65.05% ± 14.51% for control samples and 50.82% ± 28.03% for SFN and did not differ between both groups (Figure 5C).
evidence: This quantitative measurement is supported by the analysis shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Ensheathment did not differ between control and SFN groups.
source: After segmentation, the pixel count of PGP9.5 without WGA co-localization, as a correlate for ensheathment was 65.05% ± 14.51% for control samples and 50.82% ± 28.03% for SFN and did not differ between both groups (Figure 5C).

claim: The co-localization overlap between PGP9.5 and Cx43 signal was 0.53% ± 0.49% for controls.

claim: The co-localization overlap between PGP9.5 and Cx43 signal was 0.96%±2.16% for SFN.
source: Accordingly, the co-localization overlap between PGP9.5 and Cx43 signal was 0.53% ± 0.49% (for controls) and 0.96%±2.16% (for SFN) and did not differ between groups (Figure 5D).
evidence: This quantitative measurement is supported by the analysis shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Cx43 contact ratio did not differ between control and SFN groups.
source: Accordingly, the co-localization overlap between PGP9.5 and Cx43 signal was 0.53% ± 0.49% (for controls) and 0.96%±2.16% (for SFN) and did not differ between groups (Figure 5D).
evidence: This statistical comparison is supported by the analysis shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Sensory neurons and keratinocytes each formed clusters after seeding into two-compartment chambers.
source: Sensory neurons and keratinocytes each formed clusters after seeding into two-comparted chambers (Figure 6A–C).
evidence: This observation is supported by the co-culture imaging data in Figure 6.

claim: After barrier removal, neurites actively grew toward keratinocytes and established contacts within few days.
source: After barrier removal, neurites actively grew toward keratinocytes and established contacts within few days (Figure 6C and D, Figure 6—video 1).
evidence: This observation is supported by the time-lapse imaging data in Figure 6 and associated video.

claim: Neurite-keratinocyte contacts were apparent both in conditioned neuronal medium and keratinocyte medium.
source: Neurite-keratinocyte contacts were apparent, both in conditioned neuronal medium and keratinocyte medium.
evidence: This observation is based on the co-culture experiments described in the methods and results.

claim: Keratinocytes underwent terminal differentiation in neuronal medium.
source: However, keratinocytes underwent terminal differentiation in neuronal medium, while predominantly maintaining a basal state in keratinocyte medium (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).

claim: Keratinocytes predominantly maintained a basal state in keratinocyte medium.
source: However, keratinocytes underwent terminal differentiation in neuronal medium, while predominantly maintaining a basal state in keratinocyte medium (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This observation is supported by the imaging data in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Keratinocyte cell lines and iPSC cell line used for neuronal differentiation were free of mycoplasma.
source: Keratinocyte cell lines and iPSC cell line used for neuronal differentiation were free of mycoplasma and basal keratinocytes were characterized by morphology, positive cytokeratin 14 labeling, and negative cytokeratin 10 labeling (Figure 6—figure supplement 2).

claim: Basal keratinocytes were characterized by morphology, positive cytokeratin 14 labeling, and negative cytokeratin 10 labeling.
source: Keratinocyte cell lines and iPSC cell line used for neuronal differentiation were free of mycoplasma and basal keratinocytes were characterized by morphology, positive cytokeratin 14 labeling, and negative cytokeratin 10 labeling (Figure 6—figure supplement 2).

claim: Neurite-keratinocyte contacts were identified using confocal microscopy.

claim: Ensheathment was observed via lattice-SIM super-resolution microscopy in the co-culture system.

claim: Non-ensheathed neurites frequently passed in close proximity and over keratinocytes.
source: Non-ensheathed neurites frequently passed in close proximity and over keratinocytes (Figure 7D).

claim: Neurites were found growing in a gutter-like structure.

claim: Neurites were observed merging into the keratinocyte membrane.

claim: Neurites establish bouton-like contacts with keratinocytes.

claim: In iPSC-derived neurons, SYP was distributed throughout the cytoplasm and not restricted to the cytoskeleton.

claim: Only weak SYP labeling, not associated with neurite contact sites, was present in keratinocytes.

claim: Ca2+ imaging of human co-cultured sensory neurons and keratinocytes revealed spontaneous activity in both cell types in 4/7 wells.

claim: Keratinocytes showed slower and longer Ca2+ peaks.

claim: In three wells with neurites passing along keratinocytes, an increase of keratinocyte Ca2+ preceded neurite Ca2+ peaks.

claim: Ensheathment was previously described in model organisms with mono- or double-layered epidermis such as Drosophila and Danio rerio.

claim: In multi-layered mammalian and human skin, only sparse data exist from early EM studies reporting conflicting observations on ensheathment.
source: In multi-layered mammalian and human skin, only sparse data exist from early EM studies reporting conflicting observations.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of prior literature.

claim: Application of super-resolution microscopy techniques is inevitably necessary to resolve the exact course of IENF within the dense tissue of the epidermis.
source: Given the small diameter of IENF (≤1 µm) within the dense tissue of the epidermis, application of super-resolution microscopy techniques is inevitably necessary to resolve the exact course of these neurites.
evidence: This is a logical inference based on the size of IENF and the resolution limits of conventional microscopy.

claim: 'Tunneling' of IENF within keratinocytes was recently proposed via confocal microscopy in human skin.
source: Recently, 'tunneling' of IENF within keratinocytes was proposed via confocal microscopy in human skin (Talagas et al., 2020b) and via SEM in an heterologous rat-human co-culture model (Talagas et al., 2020a).
